To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a transistor model is developed for VHF switching frequencies, (2) the transistor model is used in a layout versus loss analysis to find the best device layout, (3) the best device layout is found experimentally, and (4) the best device is fabricated and validated at VHF switching frequency.

the layout of integrated lateral double-d diffused MOSFETs can be optimized for a given converter, resulting in reduced power loss, and that hot-carrier effects can be mitigated under soft switching, resulting in further loss reduction.

the layout and design of integrated transistors can be optimized to reduce power losses in dc-dc converters, that the hot-carrier safe operating area of transistors is increased under soft switching, and that the use of small gate-length devices is beneficial for VHF dc-dc converters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of integrated MOSFETs for use in VHF dc-dc converters, with the goal of reducing power loss and increasing efficiency.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimization method developed in this thesis has been successfully implemented and experimentally validated, yielding significant improvements in converter efficiency.
the optimization of integrated transistors for VHF converters is a complex problem, requiring a detailed understanding of the device physics and the application.
the optimization of a transistor layout for a given dc-dc converter application can yield a significant improvement in efficiency, even when hot carrier limits are considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of integrated lateral MOSFETs for VHF switching converters can offer significant performance improvement, but that a systematic approach must be taken for optimal performance.
the use of integrated lateral double-d diffused MOSFETs in dc-dc converters is feasible, and that the use of VHF converters is feasible, provided that device optimization is performed.
the use of integrated transistors in VHF dc-dc converters is viable, and that the design methodology developed here will allow for the optimization of such transistors for a given application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of integrated transistors for dc-dc conversion can be significantly improved by optimizing for the application.
the transistor layout is the key to reducing power losses at VHF switching frequency.
the use of integrated transistors in dc-dc converter designs is a very promising approach to reduce the size, weight, and power of VHF converters.
